slides.say: The diagonals of rectangle A B C D intersect at E. Given: C D is five centimeters, and angle B E C is a hundred twenty degrees. What is the area of the rectangle, in square centimeters?
For the area we need the length and the width. C D is five, so we still need B C. [short pause] The angle at E will lead us there.
[short pause] In a rectangle, the diagonals are equal, and they cut each other in half. So E B and E C are halves of equal diagonals, and they're equal. Triangle B E C is isosceles.
at: So E B and E C

slides.say: Its top angle is a hundred twenty. In an isosceles triangle the base angles are equal, so they share the rest equally. A hundred eighty minus a hundred twenty is sixty, and half of that is thirty. So angle E B C is thirty, and angle E C B is thirty.
at: So angle E B C is thirty

slides.say: Now look at triangle D B C. Its angle at C is ninety, because it's a corner of the rectangle. E lies on the diagonal B D, so B E and B D lie along the same line. So angle D B C is the same thirty as angle E B C.
The angles of a triangle add up to a hundred eighty, so the last angle, at D, is sixty.
Thirty, sixty, ninety: that's the gold triangle. Its sides are in the ratio a, a root three, two a. The short leg, a, is across from the thirty. Across from the thirty at B is C D, so a is five.
at: Across from the thirty at B

slides.say: The long leg is the short leg times root three. So B C is five root three.

Now the area of the whole rectangle. B C and C D are its length and its width, and they're perpendicular. So the area is five root three times five, which is twenty-five root three. Choice number three is our answer.
at: Now the area of the whole rectangle
Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: If you're not sure whether a diagonal rule is guaranteed, draw an exaggerated rectangle, very low and very wide. It's still a rectangle, and you'll see right away that its diagonals aren't perpendicular and don't cut the angles in half. So we can't assume either one in a rectangle.
And notice how a gold triangle was hiding inside the rectangle. Triangles live inside quadrilateral questions, and later in circles too. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
